newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia has expensive telephone calls - study.
newsitem.headline: Australia has expensive telephone calls - study.

text.p: Australia still remains one of the most expensive countries in which to make a local telephone call compared with some the world's leading economies, according to the latest annual NUS International Telephone Price Survey.
In the study of 12 major economies over the year to January 1, 1997, Australia was the only nation to show an increase in the price of local calls, the study showed.
The government-owned Telstra Corp has a virtual monopoly of the local call market. Its only competition so far, Optus Vision, has failed to attract many customers.
Australia is to fully deregulate its telecommunications market on July 1, 1997.

"There is little doubt that the lack of any effective competition in the lucrative local call market provides little incentive for Telstra to make any substantial reduction," NUS telecommunications manager Alan Ruff said in a statement.
"Despite a much publicised launch of the Optus local call service last June, due to various technical reasons, it is not currently a viable alternative to the majority of consumers," he said.
However, Ruff said full deregulation of the Australian market this July should result in further competitiveness and lower prices to the consumer.

"Also, the recent World Trade Organisation agreement on telecommunications should result in significant cost benefits from Australia successfully negotiating lower international prices with most of its overseas trading partners," Ruff said.

The NUS study showed Australia had the most expensive local calls with the average cost of each call at 23 Australian cents. Canada was the lowest, as it provides free local telephone calls, but charges the most for monthly rental of telephone
lines, of all the countries surveyed.
Australia was the sixth most expensive country amongst the 12 surveyed, with the average call cost of 81 Australia cents.
Germany had the most expensive national calls at A$1.33 per call, while Sweden was the lowest with 30 Australian cents.

New Zealand was the most expensive place to make an overseas call with the cost of each call at A$3.95 on average. Australia was the fourth most expensive at A$3.21, while Britain was the cheapest at A$1.32, the study showed.
The 12 countries in the survey were Australia, Belgium, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Sweden, the United Kingdom and United States.
